speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to evaluate your skin condition carefully, especially since we are looking for signs of potential malignancy. To begin, how long have you noticed the lesion, and has its appearance or size changed recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; the combination of a non-healing, crusted lesion on your penis and another on your finger, along with your heavy smoking history and failed treatments for syphilis, raises significant concern. Given the potential for malignancy, have you experienced any weight loss, night sweats, or fatigue recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of non-healing, crusted, painless lesions on both your penis and finger, despite previous treatments for syphilis and eczema, is highly suspicious for squamous cell carcinoma. Given your history of heavy smoking, what is the approximate size of these lesions in millimeters? Also, do you see any new growths or changes on your face, lips, or ears?

REQUEST TEST: Penile_Biopsy; REQUEST TEST: Finger_Biopsy
